newsitem.title: USA: Orlando rocked by four murders in tourist district.
newsitem.headline: Orlando rocked by four murders in tourist district.

text.p: Authorities in Orlando hunted for clues on Wednesday after police found the bodies of four murder victims in the nation's most popular tourist destination in just three days.

"Right now there's no direct connection between the body found this morning and the others," said Commander Steve Jones of the Orange County Sheriff's Office. "Maybe after the medical examiner gets through we'll know for sure."

The most recent victim, a woman, was found concealed in a thicket Wednesday near the first tee of the International Golf Course near the Sea World theme park. A tow truck operator and golf course workers saw a man considered a potential suspect drive away in a car with stolen Texas license plates.

On Tuesday, police had found the bodies of two women in woods nearby, near the Universal Studios Florida theme park. Police said the women apparently were not killed at the same time and that one body had been there longer than the other.
The names of the victims were not released. Police also have not said whether they were area residents or visitors.

On Monday, a man attending a beautician's convention in Orlando was killed at a hotel across from Universal Studios after he was ambushed with a female companion near the hotel's pool. The assailant bludgeoned the man to death and rolled his body into a pond, then raped the woman, who later escaped.
Both the killer/rapist and the suspect in the homicide discovered Wednesday were described as white males in their 20s.

Tourists were paying scant attention to the murders Wednesday. "You don't exactly come to Disney World to read the papers," said Ruth Anderson, who said she was vacationing at the Magic Kingdom with her family from Muncie, Indiana.
Police said they were beefing up patrols in the tourist area until they knew for sure if the murders were related.

Home to the giant Walt Disney World complex in additional to Universal Studios and Sea World, as well as other tourist attractions, the Orlando area attracts more tourists than any other U.S. vacation spot.
